log_file.description: Path to the log file where knockd will write events.

sequence_list.description: List of port-knock sequences (each sequence defines a name, ports to knock, and action(s) to trigger).

sequence.description: List of ports to knock in order (e.g., [7000, 8000, 9000]).

seq_timeout.description: Maximum time (seconds) allowed between knocks before sequence resets.

start_command.description: Command to run when the full sequence is successfully knocked (e.g., `/usr/sbin/iptables -A INPUT -s %IP% -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT`).

stop_command.description: Command to run after a delay (if sequence is 'one-shot' or to close access), e.g., `/usr/sbin/iptables -D INPUT -s %IP% -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT`.

tcpflags.description: TCP flags to match for SYN/ACK/FIN packets (e.g., 'syn', 'ack', 'fin').

synctime.description: Time (seconds) to wait before considering the knock sequence complete after last packet.

endtimeout.description: Time (seconds) before clearing the client from the knock state after a successful sequence.

use_tcp.description: Listen for TCP knock packets on this sequence.

use_udp.description: Listen for UDP knock packets on this sequence.

use_http.description: Listen for HTTP GET requests to trigger knock (requires `http_url`).

http_url.description: URL path (relative or absolute) that triggers this sequence via HTTP GET (e.g., `/knock/secret`).

http_method.description: HTTP method to expect (currently only 'GET' is supported by knockd).

http_body.description: Expected body content in the HTTP request (for advanced matching).

http_headers.description: Key-value pairs of HTTP headers to require (e.g., {'User-Agent': 'knocker/1.0'}).

interface.description: Network interface to bind to (e.g., 'eth0'). If omitted, uses default route interface.

client_ip.description: Restrict knocks to this specific source IP address.
